sources.notes: Extended Stata missing codes (.d/.i/.n/.r/.s) arrive as blanks in the extract, so DK, no answer, refusal and web skips are not separable; IAP is recovered from the ballot design. 2022 and 2024 AmeriSpeak oversample cases (sample 12, 14) carry no wtssps and are excluded. FEHOME is absent from every year. REGION in these files is the 4-region code, not the 9 Census divisions.

sources.title: National Survey of Family Growth (NSFG) 2022-2023, Female Respondent public-use file
sources.provider: National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.license: U.S. federal public-use file; NCHS data-use restrictions (see landing page) apply
sources.citation: National Center for Health Statistics. 2022-2023 National Survey of Family Growth, Female Respondent public-use data file. https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nsfg/nsfg-2022-2023-puf.htm (retrieved 2026-10-29).
sources.notes: The CSV has no value labels and the codebook PDF is not in raw/; value codings are unconfirmed, so no NSFG estimate is published yet (pipeline/registry/nsfg_codings.json). Fetch https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nsfg/codebooks/2022-2023-NSFG-FemRespPUFCodebook.pdf to unblock.

metrics.label: Ideal number of children: four or more
metrics.universe: GSS adults 18+ asked CHLDIDEL, by sex/age/religion/attendance/marital filter
metrics.definition: Weighted share answering 4, 5, 6 or '7 or more' to CHLDIDEL; 'as many as you want' is a separate valid category in the denominator; DK/NA excluded
metrics.method: wtssps-weighted ratio, Taylor-linearised design SE, logit CI; suppressed n_eff<30, exploratory 30-100
caveats: general ideal for 'a family', not own intention or expected births
2010-2018 and 2021-2024 not comparable: 'as many as you want' rises from about 7-12% (2000-2018) to 24-31% (2021-2024) of all adults after the 2021 mode change
national survey: no county or state estimate

metrics.label: Attends religious services weekly or more
metrics.definition: ATTEND 7 'every week' or 8 'several times a week'
caveats: self-reported attendance, which surveys generally find over-reported
affiliation (RELIG) and practice (ATTEND) are different measures

metrics.label: Agrees: better for man to work, woman to tend home
caveats: a role norm about families in general, not the respondent's own preference

metrics.label: Divorce should be more difficult to obtain (law)
caveats: opinion about divorce law, not marital permanence, not a probability a marriage lasts

metrics.label: Expected additional births (women)
caveats: not published until the codebook confirms the coding
